Lessons.Title: Multiplication Strategies on Ungridded Rectangles
ExplanationParagraphs: UngridDED rectangles show side lengths without individual squares. Multiply the labelled sides for area, and mark approximate subdivisions corresponding to a valid equivalent expression. Require correct units: yards×yards produces square yards.

Original warm-up four representations A–D each give18: A original3×6 gridded area split as3×2+3×4, B the same ungridded rectangle with widths2 and4, partial areas6 and12, C written expression (3×2)+(3×4), and D 3 rows of6 dots. The unlabelled vertical side of B is3. Any one representation may have a valid distinguishing feature; no unique 'wrong one'.

Source Activity1 three original ungridded rectangles: A sides9 and5 give45 unit squares, B sides6 and6 give36, and C sides8 yards and7 yards give56 square YARDS. Students mark their own rectangular partitions, which a teacher checks for area consistency.

Sort these source letters by same area and defend diagrams: A,C,L→28; B,I→42; D,F,G→24; E,K→48; H,J→36. Source teacher synthesis explicitly relates E and K, C and L, B and I, and association pair F and G. Pupils may use multiple plausible side-length representations; check more than a number.

Student section summary:6×5=30,30÷5=6,30÷6=5;7×3=21 and5×3+2×3=21. Teachers judge pupils' ungridded shading, card sorting and explanation. Publisher SVG/photo/artwork and gated Expressions for a Rectangle Cool-down not copied; Stage D and tests unrun.

KeyConcepts.Title: Ungridded area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Side labels determine area even when cells aren't drawn.

KeyConcepts.Title: Decompose ungridded rectangle
KeyConcepts.Definition: Mark a split reflecting an additive factor decomposition.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent area cards
KeyConcepts.Definition: Algebraically different multiplication expressions can calculate the same rectangle area.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Group expressions by a mathematically justified total.

KeyConcepts.Title: Regroup factors
KeyConcepts.Definition: Associative property allows factor grouping changes without changing product.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Choose a single warm-up representation as mathematically wrong.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: All four A–D total18 and 'which one doesn't belong' invites differing defensible explanations.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Judge reasoning about the representation rather than force unique wrong answer.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Classify source cards only because of a copied publisher arrangement.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Card math requires justifiable equivalent areas.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use the original mathematical expression for each card and show an equivalent rectangle.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use yards rather than square yards for8×7.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Multiplying two linear dimensions yields area units.
